He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==High school career== Stanley first attended [[Harvard-Westlake School]] in [[Studio City, Los Angeles|Studio City, California]]. As a sophomore, Stanley averaged 17.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game. In 2017, Stanley transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, California]] for his last two years of high school.{{Cite news|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/2019-five-star-cassius-stanley-transferring-to-sierra-canyon-calif|title=2019 five-star Cassius Stanley transferring to Sierra Canyon (Calif.)|work=www.usatodayhss.com|access-date=June 8, 2017}} As a senior, he averaged 17.8 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game while leading the Sierra Canyon to a 32–3 overall record. ===Recruiting=== On April 22, 2019, Stanley committed to play at [[Duke University]].{{cite May 5, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his college debut, Stanley scored 13 points to help Duke defeat [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] 68–66.{{cite news |title=No. 4 Duke edges third-ranked Kansas 68-66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168155 |access-date=November 5, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} After injuring his leg in a victory over [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]] on November 29, Stanley was ruled out indefinitely.{{cite news |title=Duke's Cassius Stanley exits Winthrop game with left leg injury |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28190795/duke-cassius-stanley-exits-winthrop-game-left-leg-injury |access-date=November 30, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 29, 2019}} However, after his leg improved quicker than expected due to rehabilitation and physical therapy, he returned to play against [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] after missing just one game.{{cite news |last1=Wiseman |first1=Steve |title=How Duke basketball's Cassius Stanley returned so quickly |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/article238129364.html |access-date=December 31, 2019 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=December 6, 2019}} On January 4, Stanley scored 20 points and five rebounds in a 95–62 win over [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168355|title=Carey scores 24 to lead No.2 Duke past Miami|publisher=ESPN|date=January 4, 2020|access-date=January 4, 2020}} On February 8, Stanley recorded 22 points and six rebounds in a 98–96 overtime victory over rival [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168364|title=Jones, Moore help No.7 Duke top rival UNC 98–96 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=February 8, 2020|access-date=February 8, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Stanley was selected to the ACC All-Freshman Team.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}} Stanley averaged 12.6 points and 4.9 rebounds per game, shooting 47 percent from the floor and 36 percent shooting from three-point range. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Duke's Cassius Stanley enters 2020 NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/04/07/cassius-stanley/ |access-date=April 7, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 7, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers / Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2020–2021)=== On November 18, 2020, Stanley was drafted in the second round, 54th overall, in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |title=Pacers Draft Cassius Stanley with 54th Overall Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-draft-cassius-stanley-54th-overall-pick |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 19, 2020 |date=November 19, 2020}} The Pacers signed Stanley to a [[two-way contract]] with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{Cite web|title=Pacers Sign Seven Players|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-seven-players|access-date=2021-03-08|website=Indiana Pacers|language=en}} He participated in the 2021 [[Slam Dunk Contest]]; however, he was eliminated following the opening round.{{Cite web|last=Ciccotelli|first=Jenna|title=2021 Slam Dunk Contest Participants: Format, Odds and Predicted Winner|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2934917-2021-slam-dunk-contest-participants-format-odds-and-predicted-winner|access-date=2021-03-08|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}} ===Detroit Pistons / Motor City Cruise (2021–2022)=== On September 28, 2021, Stanley signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|number=1442865457237671939|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has added Deividas Sirvydis, Cassius Stanley and Derrick Walton to its training camp roster.|user=Pistons_PR|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}} On October 16, 2021, Stanley was waived by the Pistons.{{cite web|title= The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has waived guards Jared Cunningham, Cassius Stanley and Derrick Walton Jr. |date=October 16, 2021|website=Twitter.com|url= https://twitter.com/Pistons_PR/status/1449549743831531527?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw |access-date=October 16, 2021}} He was added to the [[Motor City Cruise]] in October 2021.{{cite web |title=Motor City Cruise Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/motor-city-cruise-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster/n-5758151 |website=Our Sports Central |access-date=October 25, 2021 |date=October 25, 2021}} Stanley averaged 9.6 points and 4.5 rebounds per game with the Cruise. On December 25, 2021, he signed a 10-day contract with the Detroit Pistons.{{cite news |last1=Sanfoka |first1=Omari |title=Detroit Pistons sign ex-Michigan G Derrick Walton, Cassius Stanley to 10-day deals |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2021/12/25/detroit-pistons-derrick-walton-michigan-basketball-cassius-stanley/9017302002/ |access-date=December 25, 2021 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=December 25, 2021}} On January 4, 2022, Stanley was reacquired by the [[Motor City Cruise]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|access-date=January 4, 2022}} On January 8, he signed another 10-day contract with the Pistons.{{cite news |title=Pistons' Cassius Stanley: Signs second 10-day contract |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-cassius-stanley-signs-second-10-day-contract/ |access-date=January 9, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 8, 2022}} On January 18, 2022, Stanley was reacquired by the [[Motor City Cruise]]. On January 21, 2022, Stanley signed a third 10-day contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]]{{cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/01/pistons-sign-cassius-stanley-to-third-hardship-contract.html|website=hoopsrumors.com|title=Pistons Sign Cassius Stanley To Third Hardship Contract|date=January 21, 2022|access-date=January 21, 2022}} and returned to Motor City on January 31. ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2022–2023)=== On November 3, 2022, Stanley was named to the opening night roster for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|title=Vipers Finalize 2022-23 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/vipers-finalize-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895553|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} ===Hapoel Afula (2023–2024)=== On September 21, 2023, Stanley signed with [[Hapoel Afula B.C.|Hapoel Afula]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web|title=קסיוס סטנלי משלים את הסגל של עפולה|url=https://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=37224|website=Basket.co.il|date=September 21, 2023|access-date=September 21, 2023|language=Hebrew}} ===Valley Suns (2024–2025)=== On October 27, 2024, Stanley joined the [[Valley Suns]].{{cite web|title=Valley Suns Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://valley.gleague.nba.com/news/valley-suns-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 31, 2024}} ===ESSM Le Portel (2025)=== On April 9, 2025, he signed with [[ESSM Le Portel]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cassius-stanley-joins-essm-le-portel/|title=Cassius Stanley joins ESSM Le Portel|last=|first=|date=April 9, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=April 10, 2025}} ===Šiauliai (2025–2026)=== On July 23, 2025, Stanley signed with [[BC Šiauliai|Šiauliai]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL).{{Cite web|url=https://bcsiauliai.lt/saules-mieste-nba-dejimu-konkurso-dalyvis/|title=Saulės mieste – NBA dėjimų konkurso dalyvis|last=|first=|date=July 23, 2025|website=bcsiauliai.lt|publisher=|language=lt|access-date=July 23, 2025}} The club released a statement on August 21 that he did not pass his medical examination.{{cite web|title=Pranešimas apie neįsigaliojusį klubo ir žaidėjo bendradarbiavimą|url=https://bcsiauliai.lt/pranesimas-apie-neisigaliojusi-klubo-ir-zaidejo-bendradarbiavima/|website=bcsiauliai.lt|date=2025-08-21|access-date=2025-08-21|language=LT}} On December 18, 2025, Stanley recovered from injury and returned to [[BC Šiauliai|Šiauliai]].{{cite web|title=Traumą išsigydęs Stanley grįžta į "Šiaulius"|url=https://bcsiauliai.lt/trauma-issigydes-stanley-grizta-i-siaulius/|website=bcsiauliai.lt|date=2025-12-18|access-date=2025-12-28|language=lt}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
